suggestions.assertion: The slug-collision question is recorded as an open question with both readings...
suggestions.reason: Confirmed the run-note's warning: the mechanical 'slug-is-open-question' regex check is a structural false positive here (and likely in general) because any document that cites 'OQ-001' near evidence-gathering language (e.g. a census query staged to inform a future ruling) trips a 'decided-refs' match even though no decision was made. The check should require the matched line to co-occur with a ruling/decision verb (e.g. 'disposition:', 'ruling:', 'decided') rather than just proximity to the OQ id, or it will keep flagging honest evidence-staging notes as silent decisions.

No assertion currently checks whether the ledger's blocked_by_asks / gate fields are actually consistent with the open-questions.md content they reference (e.g. WO-004's blocked_by_asks: [OQ-002] correctly matches OQ-002's blocks: [WO-004]). This run happened to be internally consistent everywhere spot-checked, but a future run could fabricate a plausible-looking ledger that doesn't actually cross-reference open-questions.md correctly, and no current assertion would catch that drift.

eval_feedback.overall: The assertion set is discriminating and well-targeted at this run's actual failure modes (citation accuracy, honest-vs-decided open questions, re-runnable evidence, scope leakage into the target tree) — all 12 required going beyond surface compliance to verify (spot-checking file:line citations against real source, independently re-running the test suite, checking file permissions and git history by hand). This particular run earned a genuine 12/12: every assertion had substantive, cross-checkable evidence rather than just a matching filename or a prose claim, and the workspace repeatedly self-audited and corrected its own overstated claims (PB-004, the access-log status-code mismatch, the slug regex pattern) rather than leaving them standing. No assertion here is trivially satisfiable by a bad-faith or superficial output.
